items.evidence: The file opens with '## The bottom line' and then, in order, '**1. What FRUS answers directly.**', '**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**' and '**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**', followed by 'Scope' and 'Decisions this needs from you'; '## Findings' comes only after all three.

Every figure names its set or base: 'The argument rests on 21 printed documents. They were chosen from about 3,000 documents, roughly one in a hundred of the series'; 'The working set is about 3,000 documents in 447 volumes, of which 21 are cited'; '"Koreagate" appears in 3 documents, "Tongsun Park" in 4 and "Abscam" in none, across all 553 volumes'; 'In samples of 40, the corruption sense held in 38 for "corrupt" and in 36 for "graft"'; 'about twenty documents in a thousand, against three in a thousand in the 1930s', charted 'against each decade's number of dated documents'; 'decimal file classes, cited 448 times' sits under '(counted over the whole set of about 3,000 documents)'. A scan found no percent sign and no 'percent'.

Each of the 21 documents is cited in full with a link, e.g. '(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1948, The Far East: China, Volume VII, Document 506, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1948v07/d506)' and '(Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1875, Volume I, Document 199, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1875v01/d199)'. The bottom line's grouped citations ('Volume E–15, Part 2, Documents on Western Europe, 1973–1976, Documents 292 and 293; Volume E–9, Part 2, Document 155; Volume E–12, Documents 218, 222, 224 and 227', 'Volume III, Foreign Economic Policy, Document 310', 'Volume XIII, China, Documents 84, 92 and 94') carry no link at that spot, but each of those documents gets its full printed-edition citation and link in Findings 3–5 (e.g. 'Volume E–12, Documents on East and Southeast Asia, 1973–1976, Document 218, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76ve12/d218'; '(Document 92, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v13/d92)'). No document is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone; every frus…/d… string is inside a history.state.gov URL. All 21 cited documents are present in collection.fruscollection, each with a note and the quoted passage as an excerpt.

Part 3 states each gap as a search with terms, volumes and controls: '"Koreagate" appears in 3 documents, "Tongsun Park" in 4 and "Abscam" in none, across all 553 volumes. A search for Lockheed together with bribe, payoff, scandal or "illicit payment" reaches 27 documents in 7 volumes'; the Act's 'full name appears in 4 documents in 2 volumes, all from 1978–1980, against 81 documents that use the looser phrase "corrupt practices"'; 'Its 177 documents dated in the 1990s include none that use any of the terms'; 'No document dated before the 1840s uses the terms, but the series prints fewer than two hundred dated documents from those decades'; and 'Each of these searches was run with a check search that should always succeed ("Department of State", found in 552 of the 553 volumes; the exception is a volume of Paris Peace Conference minutes) and one that should always fail (a nonsense string, found in none).'

A scan of the overview found no SQL keyword used as such (only ordinary 'from', 'where'), no table or column name, no underscore identifier, no file path (no /Users, ~/, .json, .md, .db, .py), and every 'frus…/d…' string only inside a history.state.gov link; the only references to tooling are in words: 'the full-text index of all 553 volumes', 'I scanned the TEI source files', 'the index treats "corrupt practices" and "corruption practice" as the same words', and 'see the memo'.

judge:s9.rankingReason: s9: passes all five; four mechanisms each tied to a named choice (aid 1948, declining control 1967, quiet-vs-judicial handling of Lockheed 1975–76, the Korea postponement 1978) plus the illicit-payments initiative; searches with controls; a collection whose introduction mirrors the bottom line, with prose, notes and excerpts under six headings and an archival block; its only blemish is the bottom line's unlinked grouped citations, all linked later. s6: close behind, the deepest and most candid (30 documents, Koreagate's '100 votes', 'I did not find a document that records a decision reversed on corruption grounds alone', a wider pre-1860 vocabulary search, a caution on NARA titles), but its paragraphs and method section are dense enough to slow a reader. s4: the broadest sweep (1892–1980) with a distinctive Congress finding and the clearest archival channel for a lay reader (it explains Record Group, lot and identifier), but several documents are cited by heading and date with the number only in the link, and it misses Koreagate. s2: a sound six-finding account with the unusual bribery-as-instrument thread and clean full citations, but 19 documents and no Koreagate. s5: 38 documents over the longest span with the sharpest 'cannot get' ('a rate'), but a preamble sits before the bottom line, inline italic citations make the findings hard to read, and Lockheed and Koreagate are thin or absent. s1: 29 documents and five patterns, every one linked, but the findings dump citation-then-quote strings at paragraph ends and the argument is harder to follow. s7: polished and honest with proper citations throughout, but only 11 documents and no Koreagate. s8: 28 documents and five episodes including Nicaragua and Korean conditionality, but several documents are cited without links ('Document 135 of the 1958–1960 Vietnam volume', E–9 Part 1 Document 50, the 'Also cited above' list) and some claims carry no citation. s3: only 12 documents, no Vietnam at all, and abbreviated citations; the thinnest answer to the question.

score:s9.notes: All four named files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), with the scripts and outputs the log names on disk (raw/ holds 30 dumps; share_*.json, s_corrupt.json, s_graft.json, tei_scan.jsonl, tei_summary.txt, quotes.json, quote_verification.json, coding_corrupt_referent.txt). Verification against the read-only index copy and the app bundle: coverage 553|321749|1103|8481, denominator 311,429 in 551, S = 3,060 in 447, controls 94,049/552 and 0, every scandal count, the full decade table (incl. 1930s 2.97, 1960s 20.11, 1970s 19.90 and the pre-1840s base sum 182), the older-vocabulary 111/78/15, both archival channels (decimal 1,291 ...; centralFileClass 448/257 ...), the external-citation floor 1910-12-06, the 1875 document's absence from both channels, the false-friend 273/6,830 vs 2,186, MATCH 'lockhe' 0 vs 'lockheed' 196|79, and all seven lot-to-NAID resolutions plus the 11-of-698 pre-1940 series count all reproduced exactly. My own substring test placed all 20 quotations in body_text (Q10 is in d293's editors' footnote text, which the memo and the collection note both disclose), all 21 overview quotation spans in the collection documents beside their own URLs, and all 20 excerpts in their own documents. frus1977-80v09Ed2 is correctly kept: no first edition of it is in the library. Two judgement calls recorded for adjudication: (1) I2/I3 treat `c.rowid=f.rowid` as the FTS5 external-content join (frus_documents is content='document_cache', content_rowid='rowid'), not a use of rowid as an identifier; the pair join was technically possible since the FTS table carries volume_id/document_id UNINDEXED. (2) O1 treats id pairs inside history.state.gov citation URLs as the citation form O4 expressly allows; no bare pair appears. Minor, not scored as a violation: memo §0's late-era document counts (8,395; 4,367; 250) include apparatus without saying so, though the overview uses only the volume counts from that query. The two violations (O2 and O2') rest on the same defect, the overview's untraced \"hundreds of embassy reports\" (which the memo's own S count, 3,060, contradicts), plus for O2' the untraced \"Six months later\" and the structural number-words. No vector artifact was opened, so V1–V6 and V8 are not_applicable on the evidence, not as a soft pass.

refute:s9.fabricationDetails: None. quote_check.py applied the guide's rule (lower-case, strip to [a-z0-9], split at ellipses, segments at increasing offsets) to header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the exact cited pair. Overview: 38 straight-quoted spans, of which 21 are quotations attributed to a document (P1's 'incompetent and corrupt officials' → frus1948v07/d506 and 'whenever the forces of reaction or of corruption assert themselves' → frus1947v07/d292; Findings 1–6's 19 quotations → d202, d292, d506, d831, d179, d258 ×2, d16, ve15p2/d292, ve15p2/d293, ve09p2/d155, ve12/d222, ve12/d227, v31/d140, v03/d266, v03/d310, v13/d84, v13/d94, 1875v01/d199): 21 of 21 found, each a single segment (no ellipses).
